summary: The note recounts how 45-year-old software developer Michael Thompson survived a severe heart attack on September 15, 2023, near Nashville, Tennessee. His wife Susan's quick 911 call, his family's support, and neighborhood generosity helped his recovery. The scare led the whole family to adopt healthier habits, showing how family and community shape recovery and lifestyle change.
one_line: Michael Thompson survives a 2023 heart attack, and his family and neighbors support a recovery that transforms the whole family's lifestyle.
key_facts: Michael Thompson, 45, had a severe heart attack (myocardial infarction) on September 15, 2023.
Michael is a software developer and the attack began around lunchtime on a Thursday while he was working.
His symptoms were overwhelming chest pressure and intense nausea, which he first mistook for indigestion.
His wife Susan Thompson called 911 as Michael slumped into a chair, pale and short of breath.
The Thompsons live on the outskirts of Nashville, Tennessee; paramedics arrived within minutes and took him to the nearest hospital.
The Thompsons have two children: Emma, 12, and Lucas, 9, who made get-well-soon cards for his hospital room.
Before the attack Michael worked long hours, ate fast food on the go, and barely exercised; doctors linked these habits to the heart attack.
Brian and Linda Hartley, family friends, organized a roster to drive Michael to cardiac rehabilitation appointments.
Neighbor John Davies, 57, took daily walks with Michael as part of his new exercise regimen.
Neighbors delivered heart-healthy meals daily after Michael returned home.
Susan researched and prepared nutritious meals, took up evening jogs, and the children joined soccer and dance classes.
Michael's weekend barbecues now feature grilled vegetables and lean meats; his energy levels soared and medical reports showed significant progress.
